newsitem.title: CROATIA: Zagrebacka leads Croatian stocks to higher realms.
newsitem.headline: Zagrebacka leads Croatian stocks to higher realms.

text.p: Blue chip Zagrebacka Banka led Croatian stocks higher amid strong buying on Wednesday, and the market was seen rising further this week.
Gainers beat losers 15 to one, with volume and turnover surging to levels unseen in the past weeks of slow trade.
"It has been a very lively day. I expect most prices to continue firming tomorrow and the next day," a major trader told Reuters.
He ascribed this to revived investor interest in Croatia spurred by Zagrebacka after it released better than expected 1996 pre-tax figures and was awarded a first-ever credit rating on Tuesday.
The bank's ordinary stock closed 170 kuna higher at a record 2,020 kuna on volume of 7,717 units, after peaking at 2,080 kuna.
It also pulled up the bearer D shares to 850 from 800 kuna and preferred E series to 1,016 from 999 kuna, though they were traded on smaller volumes.
Zagrebacka's global depositary receipts (GDRs), issued at 10 to a share, hit their own record of $35 on London's Seaq. They were floated at $8.50 each in June last year.
"This is a normal reaction after yesterday's results and rating news," the trader added.
As buying interest spilled over into other issues, drugs firm Pliva added 3.33 percent to 465 kuna on volume of 5,988 shares.

"This price, which I think is very good for Pliva, could move up if it beats market rumours about disappointing 1996 results," said one analyst. The company is to release last year's results later this month.
Other gainers included hoteliers and food stocks, all of which are beginning to recover from recent low levels.
Newcomer Varazdinska Banka traded only 10 ordinary shares, though they rose to 46,000 from 42,025 kuna.
Food concern Podravka, with 9,051 shares sold, was the most active issue. It gained one kuna to 300.

"Once this psychological barrier is overcome, which should happen in the next few days, most of the shares will go. But (Podravka) still seems to need some impulse to pierce it," said the first trader.
He pointed to confectioner Kras as another stock which could benefit from a positive signal, such as a long-awaited investment accord with the EBRD.
It rose 30 kuna or 7.41 percent to 450 kuna with 480 shares sold, but its further upward move seemed doubtful.
The only loser was hotelier Arenaturist, down 30 kuna to 150 from late in February on volume of 30 shares.
